status_summary: The July 4, 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) gave CBP about $46.55 billion for border infrastructure and wall plus about $6.17 billion for border security technology, per CRS, which matches the Mandate's request for mandatory wall funding. DHS and CBP announced about $4.5 billion in first construction contracts in autumn 2025 (about 230 miles of Smart Wall barrier and nearly 400 miles of technology). Axios reported on 2026-06-21 that about 10 percent of the planned primary wall was complete, that DHS Secretary Mullin said it would be finished within a year and that CBP's commissioner said the end of 2027. Military national defense areas along the southern border cover between one-third and one-half of the border as of August 2026, per the Christian Science Monitor, and a DOJ opinion dated 2026-08-14 addressed military arrests just outside them. Most of the planned wall remains unbuilt.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14165 directs Defense and Homeland Security to deploy and build temporary and permanent barriers on the southern border.
Presidential memorandum directs U.S. Northern Command to plan to seal the border and repel invasion, with a Unified Command Plan revision due in 10 days.

P.L. 119-21 enacted with about $46.55 billion for CBP border infrastructure and wall, about $6.17 billion for border security and technology, and about $5 billion for facilities (CRS cautions component figures do not fully sum).

DHS and CBP announce about $4.5 billion across 10 construction projects covering more than 230 miles of barrier and nearly 400 miles of technology in Texas, Arizona, New Mexico and California; two waivers cover the San Diego and El Paso sectors. Contracts were awarded in late September 2025.

P.L. 119-98 provides about $3.45 billion for scanning equipment, air and marine assets, surveillance technology and biometric entry and exit; no new wall construction line was identified in CRS's summary.

Axios reports about 10 percent of the planned primary wall is complete and about 698 miles remain per a CBP spokesperson; Secretary Mullin says completion by about June 2027, while CBP's commissioner cites the end of 2027.

DOJ issues an opinion (requested by the Pentagon in April 2026) that arrests just outside a national defense area are lawful under the Posse Comitatus Act; the Monitor reports 161 temporary detentions by Joint Task Force-Southern Border.
